slots_and_copies.name: global_header
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Loaded first and validated by FUN_080180b4 (magic compare + sum16-to-zero). If invalid, FUN_08018064 creates a default header and FUN_080178a0 blanks the first block of every slot. No backup or mirror copy exists.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: EEPROM blocks 2-21. Loaded by FUN_08017f30(slot=0) into the shared 160-byte heap buffer at manager+0x10; validity flag at manager+0x2C+0 written by FUN_08017ee8 as (sum16 over 160 bytes == 0); descriptor at manager+0x14+0 activated or zeroed by FUN_080179c0. Independent slot, not a copy of any other slot.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_1
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: EEPROM blocks 22-41. Same load/validate/activate path as slot_0 with slot index 1 (validity at manager+0x2C+4, descriptor at manager+0x14+8). Independent slot, not a copy of any other slot.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_2
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: EEPROM blocks 42-61. Same load/validate/activate path as slot_0 with slot index 2 (validity at manager+0x2C+8, descriptor at manager+0x14+16). Independent slot, not a copy of any other slot.

slots_and_copies.name: unused_tail
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: EEPROM blocks 62-63. No traced reader or writer addresses this range; all 0xFF in both samples.

checksums.name: header_sum16_negated
checksums.formula_detail: Additive 16-bit sum (FUN_08018028: uVar1 = *p + uVar1 & 0xFFFF per u16 word) over the whole 16-byte header. Store (FUN_08017fa8/FUN_08018064): zero the word at offset 0x0E, compute s=sum of all 8 words, store (-s)&0xFFFF at 0x0E. Validation (FUN_080180b4): total sum == 0. IMPORTANT byte-order note: the algorithm enum has no big-endian variant; at the file level the words must be interpreted BIG-ENDIAN for the rule to hold (verified on both samples), while little-endian fails on both (total 0x01FE, computed 0x7F01 != stored 0x80FF). The decompiled code sums RAM u16 words as assembled MSB-first by the EEPROM read driver FUN_08047504. 'sum16_le' is used here only as the closest enum value for a 16-bit additive sum; see formula_detail and SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.2 for the byte-order caveat.

checksums.name: slot_sum16_negated_candidate
checksums.formula_detail: Same FUN_08018028 routine applied by FUN_08017ee8 over the full 160-byte slot (80 words): slot is valid iff total sum == 0 mod 65536. By header analogy a writer stores (-sum of other 79 words)&0xFFFF in one slot word, hypothesised to be the last word (slot offset 0x9E), but no slot writer exists in the traced corpus so the stored offset is unproven. File-level word byte order assumed big-endian as for the header; all-0x00/0xFF blank data cannot distinguish byte order. Blank samples sum to 0xFFB4 (invalid) for every slot. See the header checksum entry for the enum/byte-order caveat.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer engine for the EEPROM serial window 0x0D000000. Programs DMA3 source/destination/control via literal-pool pointers, sets count&0xFFFF|0x80000000 (enable), busy-waits on control bit 0x8000, saves/restores interrupt/DMA enable. Used for both directions; role 'write' is the enum's closest fit for a bidirectional DMA primitive.

EEPROM read one 8-byte block: bounds-checks block vs descriptor+4, sends start+read-opcode+address bitstream (MSB first, width from descriptor+8) via FUN_08047484, clocks back 0x44 halfwords, reassembles 4 u16 MSB-first. Returns 0 on success.

EEPROM write one 8-byte block: expands 4 u16 + address into serial bitstream (addr_bits+0x43 halfwords) to 0x0D000000 via FUN_08047484, then polls EEPROM data line (0x0D000000 & 1) with timer-based timeout (wrap 0xE4, limit 0x88) until write-complete.
Wrapper: calls FUN_080475c8(block, src, 1), always requesting the write-complete wait.
EEPROM verify one block: reads back via FUN_08047504 and compares 4 u16 against source; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch. Role is verify; 'read' is the closest enum value.

EEPROM access-mode set (called with 4 from FUN_08018220; other branches for 0x40/other). No true erase exists for this EEPROM path; mode-set is listed with role 'erase' only because the enum lacks a 'mode' value. Exact register fields unresolved (literal-pool values not in workspace).

Enter EEPROM access: saves WAITCNT-class global, zeroes control global, calls FUN_0804743c(4). Brackets every multi-block transfer together with FUN_0801826c (restore). Role is session bracketing, not data transfer.
Leave EEPROM access: restores the global saved by FUN_08018220. Session bracketing only.

Read N blocks: FUN_08018220 enter, per-block FUN_08047504 with retry counter starting at 3 (up to 4 attempts/block), dst+=8, block+=1, FUN_0801826c leave. Returns (last_error==0). Callgraph lists no edges for this function; edges are from decompiled body text.

Write N blocks with per-block verify: FUN_080475b4 write then FUN_08047728 verify, retrying while either fails. Traced calls only ever pass count 2 (header) or 1 (slot first-block blanking); no traced call writes a full 20-block slot.
sum16: sums (byte_len>>1) u16 words masking to 16 bits after each add. The only checksum routine in the save path; no CRC/XOR routine exists in the traced save functions.
Create default header: memcpy 16-byte ROM template (_DAT_080180b0) into header mirror via FUN_08013828, store -(sum16) at mirror+0xE, write blocks 0-1 via FUN_08018198.
Validate header: read blocks 0-1 via FUN_0801811c; return 0 if read fails or sum16(mirror,0x10)!=0; else byte-compare 8 magic bytes vs ROM constant pcRam08018118 and return match.

Flush header if changed: read EEPROM header to stack, zero mirror+0xE, recompute and store -sum16 at mirror+0xE, compare mirror vs readback as 4 u32, write blocks 0-1 via FUN_08018198 only if different. Only traced checksummed writer; mutates only the checksum field.
Load one slot: FUN_0801811c(slot*0x14+2, 0x14, *(manager+0x10)) reads 20 blocks into the shared heap slot buffer.
Slot validity: writes *(manager+0x2C+4*slot) = (FUN_08018028(slot_buffer,0xA0)==0).
Zero the shared 160-byte slot buffer in RAM (FUN_080137a0 fill). RAM-side blanking only; EEPROM blanking is done by FUN_080178a0 via FUN_08018198.

Save-manager init/load orchestrator: allocates slot buffer (FUN_080135d0(0xA0) -> manager+0x10), validates header, on invalid creates default header + blanks each slot's first block, reads selector byte manager+10 via FUN_0801d04c, then FUN_08017eac loads all slots. No caller in callgraph or body text (unrecovered jumptable entry); boot-init trigger is inferred.
Load all slots: for slot 0..2 calls FUN_08017f30, FUN_08017ee8, FUN_080179c0.

Post-load per-slot activation: if validity flag==0, zero 8-byte descriptor at manager+0x14+8*slot; else set manager+0x3C=slot buffer, manager+0x40=0 and call func_0x0802c164(descriptor), which is not in the decompiled corpus.

Header-flush caller: FUN_0801bd2c(); FUN_08017fa8(); FUN_0801bd50(). The two bracket wrappers call func_0x08044420/func_0x080443f0, absent from the corpus; trigger context unknown; no caller in callgraph.

fields.name: header_magic
fields.update_mechanism: Installed from ROM template by FUN_08018064 (memcpy FUN_08013828 from _DAT_080180b0); carried unchanged by FUN_08017fa8 header flush. FUN_080180b4 byte-compares these 8 bytes against ROM constant pcRam08018118 on load.
fields.evidence: FUN_080180b4 8-byte compare loop (iVar4<8) and FUN_08018064 template copy in ghidra/decompiled.c; identical bytes at file offset 0 in both .sav samples (see SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.4 output).

fields.name: header_byte_08_counter_candidate
fields.update_mechanism: No traced field-specific writer. Installed by the FUN_08018064 template copy and carried by the FUN_08017fa8 flush (which recomputes the checksum at 0x0E). High byte of header word 4 (big-endian word 0x0485 -> 0x0385 between captures).
fields.evidence: Only differing header byte besides 0x0C between the two samples; decremented by 1 while byte 0x0C incremented by 1 (checksum-neutral pair). PACKET.md mutation probe at 0x8 confirms this byte is integrity-covered. Semantics unknown; counter-like behaviour is a hypothesis. RAM mirror offset +0x08; absolute RAM address not recoverable from workspace.

fields.name: header_byte_09_constant_candidate
fields.update_mechanism: Template copy / header flush only; no traced semantic reader or writer. Low byte of header word 4.
fields.evidence: Constant 0x85 in both samples; no function in ghidra/decompiled.c accesses mirror+0x09 individually.

fields.name: header_byte_0a_selector_candidate
fields.update_mechanism: Template copy / header flush carry the byte. On load FUN_080178a0 reads *(u8*)(manager+10), passes it to FUN_0801d04c (which stores it and indexes a table by value*4) and copies it to a global byte.
fields.evidence: FUN_080178a0: func_0x0801d04c(*(undefined1*)(_DAT_0801790c+10)) and copy to _DAT_08017910+_DAT_08017914; FUN_0801d04c indexes param*4. Index-like use is static; current-slot/profile selection semantics inferred. RAM mirror offset +0x0A.

fields.name: header_byte_0b_reserved
fields.update_mechanism: Template copy / header flush only; read only as part of the checksummed 16-byte region. High byte of header word 5 (big-endian 0x0000).
fields.evidence: Zero in both samples; no individual access in decompiled.c.

fields.name: header_byte_0c_counter_candidate
fields.update_mechanism: No traced field-specific writer. Template copy / header flush carry the byte. High byte of header word 6 (big-endian 0x0000 -> 0x0100 between captures).
fields.evidence: Incremented by 1 between captures while byte 0x08 decremented by 1, leaving the header checksum (0xFF80) unchanged in both files. Counter-like; semantics unknown. RAM mirror offset +0x0C.

fields.name: header_byte_0d_reserved
fields.update_mechanism: Template copy / header flush only; read only as part of the checksummed region. Low byte of header word 6.
fields.evidence: Zero in both samples; no individual access in decompiled.c.

fields.name: header_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_08017fa8: zero mirror+0x0E, compute FUN_08018028 sum16 over 16 bytes, store (-sum)&0xFFFF. FUN_08018064: store -sum16 after template copy (no explicit pre-zero). Validation: FUN_080180b4 requires total sum == 0. Type is 'unknown' in this JSON only because the schema enum has no u16 big-endian value; the on-media word is big-endian (see evidence).
fields.evidence: Python verification (SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.4): BE words sum to 0x0000 in both files; stored BE 0xFF80 == computed (-sum of other 7 BE words) 0xFF80 in both files; LE interpretation fails in both (sum 0x01FE, computed 0x7F01). Decompiled proof in FUN_08018028/FUN_08017fa8/FUN_08018064/FUN_080180b4. RAM mirror offset +0x0E.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_080180b4 magic compare fails -> header rejected -> FUN_08018064 default header written and slot first blocks re-zeroed (blank state). Distinguishes magic failure from checksum failure.
Header sum != 0 -> FUN_080180b4 rejects -> blank re-init and save rewrite. Reproduces the PACKET.md probe at 0x8 (integrity_check_confirmed).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change 0x04 -> 0x05 and repair header checksum at 0x0E (big-endian -sum of other 7 words)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Header must be accepted (magic intact, sum 0). Any gameplay delta or later rewrite of byte 0x08 attributes semantics to it; survival across a save cycle marks it as passive data. Primary test of the counter hypothesis.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change 0x00 -> 0x02 and repair header checksum at 0x0E
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Header accepted. Run separately from the offset-8 test to determine whether bytes 0x08 and 0x0C are independent fields or a compensating pair maintained by an untraced writer.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set selector byte to 0x01, then 0x02, then 0x03 (three runs), repairing header checksum each time
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If byte 0x0A is the current-slot selector (FUN_080178a0 -> FUN_0801d04c value*4 table index), 1/2 select slots 1/2 and 3 tests out-of-range handling (clamp/ignore/crash). No file rewrite predicted on load itself.
Total header sum != 0 with all data bytes intact -> rejection and blank rewrite. Proves the stored word participates in validation.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Fill slot 0 (0x10-0xAF) with a known ramp pattern and apply the candidate slot checksum repair at 0xAE (big-endian -sum of other 79 words)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If slot validity is sum-to-zero with the stored word last, FUN_08017ee8 flags slot 0 valid and FUN_080179c0 activates its descriptor instead of zeroing it (game offers/loads slot 0). If still invalid, repeat the repair at alternate candidate word offsets (0x10, 0x18) to locate the stored word.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Copy a repaired populated slot 0 image over slot 1 (0xB0-0x14F) with candidate checksum repair at 0x14E
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Slot 1 becomes independently valid/selectable, proving slots are independent 160-byte regions with no cross-slot coupling and no generation counter.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change one deep slot-0 payload byte 0xFF -> 0x00 in an otherwise blank save, no repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Negative control: slot 0 sum changes 0xFFB4 -> 0xFFB3, invalid either way, so no observable change is predicted. Proves blank-state slot bytes are not individually interpreted.
No traced reader addresses blocks 62-63, so no observable change and no rewrite predicted. Any reaction reveals an untraced tail consumer.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change constant byte 0x85 -> 0x86 and repair header checksum at 0x0E
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Header accepted. Any gameplay/visual delta attributes semantics to byte 0x09; no delta strengthens the static-template-byte reading.

open_questions: No full populated-slot writer exists in the traced 294-function corpus: the only slot EEPROM writes are the 1-block blanking writes in FUN_080178a0. The gameplay serialisation of a 160-byte slot, its internal field layout, and the exact stored-checksum word offset inside a slot (hypothesised last word) are unknown.
Both .sav samples are blank-initialised state (valid header, slots invalid with sum 0xFFB4). No populated slot exists to map gameplay fields (progress, counters, unlocks) against.

Semantics of header bytes 0x08 (0x04->0x03), 0x09 (constant 0x85) and 0x0C (0x00->0x01) are unknown; 0x08/0x0C changed as a checksum-neutral pair with no traced field writer. Confirmation that byte 0x0A is the current-slot selector (vs another profile index) requires a populated-slot test.

Absolute RAM addresses are unrecoverable from the workspace: Ghidra _DAT_0801xxxx values are ROM literal-pool addresses and the pointed-to manager base / heap slot-buffer addresses are not included. Only manager-relative offsets (+0x00 header mirror, +0x10 slot buffer pointer, +0x14 descriptors, +0x2C validity flags, +0x3C/+0x40 activation) are known.

Entry callers of FUN_080178a0 and FUN_0802c960 are absent (unrecovered jumptables), and FUN_0801bd2c/FUN_0801bd50/func_0x08044420/func_0x080443f0/func_0x0802c164 are not in the decompiled corpus, so trigger contexts for load and header flush are unknown.

EEPROM descriptor values (block count at descriptor+4, address-bit count at descriptor+8, used by FUN_08047504/FUN_080475c8) were not observed; 64 blocks / 6 address bits are inferred from the 512-byte file and stream lengths.

ROM template bytes at _DAT_080180b0 beyond the magic, and the stored form of the magic constant at pcRam08018118, are not in the workspace; this leaves a residual intra-block word-order caveat for RAM-mirror byte offsets (file offsets are unaffected and authoritative).

FUN_08018064 does not explicitly zero offset 0x0E before summing (unlike FUN_08017fa8); correctness on real hardware implies the ROM template checksum word is consistent with that, but the template bytes needed to confirm this are absent.
